How camps work under NCAA rules

All college athletic camps must operate under strict NCAA guidelines that mandate open-access policies with only age and capacity limits . This means camps cannot be used as exclusive gatekeeping tools—any athlete meeting basic eligibility criteria may attend. Colleges advertise these camps through their official websites and email lists, making them visible to families actively exploring recruitment opportunities.

The reason this transparency exists: athletic camps serve a legitimate educational purpose alongside their function as revenue generators. As Renee Lopez explains in the podcast , coaches use camps to evaluate prospective athletes in a controlled setting while generating funds that support scholarship budgets and program operations. This dual reality is often missed by families who assume a camp invitation automatically signals serious recruitment interest.
Why a camp invite is evaluation, not recruitment

Receiving a camp invitation should be understood as an opportunity to be assessed, not a guarantee of interest . Colleges send invitations broadly to build their talent pipeline and generate revenue. A single invite, without additional contact from a coach, does not indicate you are on a recruiting list or a scholarship prospect.

If one caregiver is negligent, disrespectful, or unreliable, the business reputation collapses. For a single owner managing multiple accounts and employees, that exposure was unacceptable. As Killeen explains in the episode , he needed a model where he could succeed without building and managing a large payroll team.
Why Oasis Senior Advisors Solved the Problem

Oasis operates on a completely different framework: the consultant (Killeen himself) is the primary point of contact and decision-maker —no hourly staff running the core service. His job is to listen to families, tour communities with them, and guide them toward the right placement. The business scales through expertise and judgment, not labor management.

Three observations that reveal authentic culture

The most critical assessment begins the moment you enter the community. Staff interactions with residents tell you everything about the underlying culture—whether people are treated as individuals worthy of respect or merely processed through a facility. Pay attention to how staff members greet residents, how they listen, and whether residents seem engaged or withdrawn.

Equally important, observe staff dynamics with each other. If team members interact with genuine warmth and professionalism, that culture flows directly to resident care. Tension or disrespect among staff signals deeper problems that will affect your loved one's daily experience.

Never skip the meal —it's not a minor detail. Seniors eat breakfast, lunch, and dinner at these communities, so the quality and presentation of food matters enormously. Taste what your loved one will eat. If the food is mediocre, uninspiring, or poorly prepared, that's a red flag about overall standards and care attention to detail.
